title: A bug filed into an active sprint without touches is refused or warned at new
goal: backlog.py new bug --sprint SP of an active sprint without --touch exits 2 naming --touch, and files nothing (the bug is filed unsprinted or with --touch; gate g1), so a worker's filed bug is ready to claim. Answers SP-evkj4avq, where BG-rqkc66vj and BG-6i6pdahh were filed into the sprint with no touches and the orchestrator added them before the claim.

run: import json,os,subprocess,sys,tempfile; t=tempfile.mkdtemp(); os.makedirs(t+"/_backlog"); open(t+"/_backlog/SP-testtest.json","w").write(json.dumps({"id":"SP-testtest","kind":"sprint","title":"t","status":"active","goal":"g"})); p=subprocess.run([sys.executable,"_tools/backlog.py","--root",t,"new","bug","--title","b","--severity","S3","--repro","python3 -c \"import sys; sys.exit(1)\"","--sprint","SP-testtest"],capture_output=True,text=True); sys.exit(0 if p.returncode==2 and "--touch" in p.stderr+p.stdout and os.listdir(t+"/_backlog")==["SP-testtest.json"] else 1)

gates.question: What does new bug --sprint do for an active sprint when no --touch is given?
options: refuse with exit 2 naming --touch; the bug is filed unsprinted or with --touch
file it with a warning that done refuses every file
gates.recommendation: refuse with exit 2 naming --touch; the bug is filed unsprinted or with --touch
gates.answer: refuse with exit 2 naming --touch; the bug is filed unsprinted or with --touch
